title: ALP Bootstrap Facts v1
description: Validates metadata/bootstrap.json -- the single source of truth for the Zephyr-workspace-assembly FACTS scripts/bootstrap.sh, scripts/bootstrap.ps1, and Python Tan read today (issue #917). Facts only; control flow (ZEPHYR_BASE reuse/rejection, venv idempotency, .west branching) stays as CODE in each executor -- this schema deliberately has no step/action shape. scripts/check_bootstrap_manifest.py is the drift gate that keeps this file, west.yml's zephyr revision, and each CI workflow's own Zephyr pin in lockstep (see that script's own module docstring for the full list of checks it runs).

_comment.description: The file's own contract statement: facts only, no control-flow DSL. Kept as a real JSON field (not a comment) since JSON has no native comment syntax.

schemaVersion.description: This manifest's own contract version, independent of board.yaml's schema_version or the build-plan's schemaVersion.

version.description: The Zephyr revision alp-sdk is verified against -- MUST equal the `revision:` under `- name: zephyr` in west.yml (check_bootstrap_manifest.py enforces this, and separately that neither bootstrap script hardcodes this value itself).

requirementsPath.description: Workspace-relative POSIX-style path to Zephyr's own Python requirements file, installed into the workspace venv.

pythonMinVersion.description: Zephyr's REAL build-time Python floor -- the `PYTHON_MINIMUM_REQUIRED` this pinned Zephyr revision's own `cmake/modules/python.cmake` hardcodes, which `west build`'s CMake configure enforces regardless of what bootstrap accepted. Deliberately a SEPARATE key from `prerequisites.pythonMinVersion`, not a replacement for it (issue #1078): that key is host-universal -- every backend's build-plan emission runs `alp_project.py`, not just Zephyr's, so raising it to 3.12 would refuse a Yocto-only or metadata-only host that never touches Zephyr, and 3.12 is unreachable via `apt-get install python3` on the Ubuntu 22.04 / Debian 12 hosts this repo's own docs recommend. This key exists so the SDK -- not a hand-typed constant in a consumer -- stays the single source of truth for the Zephyr-scoped number: `scripts/check_bootstrap_manifest.py` derives the real value straight from the pinned Zephyr checkout's `cmake/modules/python.cmake` (`git show <rev>:cmake/modules/python.cmake`) and fails if this field disagrees, so a Zephyr version bump that changes its own floor cannot drift silently the way a hand-typed copy would. Neither `scripts/bootstrap.sh` nor `scripts/bootstrap.ps1` reads or enforces this value today -- both still gate only on `prerequisites.pythonMinVersion` (a bootstrap-of-the-bootstrap floor check has to run before Zephyr's own CMake ever does); a project-aware executor enforcing this Zephyr-scoped floor (e.g. tan, once it reads this field) is the still-outstanding consumer-side half of issue #1078, gated on tan v0.6.0 (tan-cli#270).

dirName.description: Workspace-relative venv directory name (e.g. '.venv' -- a leading dot is fine, the literal path segments '.' and '..' are not). Constrained non-empty and slash-free, and rejects exactly '.'/'..': bootstrap.sh interpolates this raw into a workspace path that a later `rm -rf` can target (recreate-on-broken-venv) -- an empty, '.', or '..' value would turn that into a workspace-wide delete.

posixBinDir.description: Executable subdirectory name inside the venv on POSIX (Linux/macOS/git-bash). Same path-safety constraint as dirName for defense in depth -- also interpolated into venv paths, though today's `rm -rf` target is built from dirName alone, not this field.

windowsBinDir.description: Executable subdirectory name inside the venv on native Windows. Same path-safety constraint as dirName for defense in depth -- also interpolated into venv paths, though today's `rm -rf` target is built from dirName alone, not this field.

prerequisites.description: Mirrors the CURRENT scripts' own prereq checks (bootstrap.sh checks the posix list on Linux, which includes ninja since #971 -- Zephyr's default CMake generator on every host, not just Windows -- and the narrower macos list on Darwin, see that key's own description below; bootstrap.ps1 checks the windows list, plus a separate python >= pythonMinVersion check) -- recorded faithfully, not silently unified, since the scripts genuinely check different tool sets today (posix and windows track different binary names for the same interpreter -- python3 vs python). Neither script can read THIS list to perform its own prereq check (that would be circular: the check exists to confirm python/jsonschema-free tooling is present before this JSON can be parsed with confidence) -- instead scripts/check_bootstrap_manifest.py asserts each script's hardcoded copy agrees with the list it's declared against byte-for-byte (bootstrap.sh's canonical REQUIRED_BINS against posix, its Darwin-branch REQUIRED_BINS reassignment against macos, bootstrap.ps1's $Prereqs against windows), so a drift on any of the three fails the gate instead of going unnoticed.

macos.description: The EFFECTIVE macOS prerequisite set -- a narrower subset of `posix` (drops `xz`/`wget`: bsdtar decompresses .xz in-process on macOS, and the pinned Zephyr SDK's setup.sh only hard-checks for `wget` on its linux-* host branch -- see scripts/bootstrap.sh's Darwin-branch REQUIRED_BINS comment for the full rationale). A separate declared key, not `posix` minus a hardcoded exclusion list, so bootstrap.sh's Darwin-branch REQUIRED_BINS reassignment has its own byte-for-byte comparison target -- without one, that reassignment could silently drift (add or drop a tool) with nothing to catch it, the same hole prerequisites.posix/windows close for the non-Darwin lists.

install.description: The single-source-of-truth install command for each prerequisites.* tool (issue #949) -- one shell command per tool, not per bare package name, so a doctor/doc/script site can print it verbatim. Deliberately keyed by linux/macos/windows -- NOT by a single `posix` key the way prerequisites.posix itself is -- because a `sudo apt-get install`-shaped command is Debian-family-specific and a `brew install`-shaped command is macOS-specific; one `posix` key cannot hold both without silently picking one distro's package manager as the de-facto POSIX standard, which is exactly why the issue #949 body itself already listed `posix` and `macos` separately rather than folding them together. These three OS keys instead mirror nativeLibHints' own OS key set immediately below, which hit the identical apt-vs-brew problem for the same reason. `install.macos` and `install.windows` each still carry ONE flat tool->command map (macOS has exactly one relevant package manager -- brew -- and so does native Windows -- winget), and each object's tool-name KEYS must exactly equal `prerequisites.posix` (macos) or are windows' own completeness rule below. `install.linux` (issue #1464) is DIFFERENT: it is keyed by PACKAGE MANAGER, not by tool -- `install.linux.apt` / `install.linux.dnf`, each an inner tool->command map -- because 'linux' is not one target the way 'macos'/'windows' are: a `sudo apt-get install`-shaped command that's correct on Debian/Ubuntu is either absent or wrong on a host with no apt at all (Fedora/Arch/Rocky measured byte-identical to Debian before this fix), and a bare `posix`-shaped or `linux`-shaped single command can never hold more than one package manager's shape without silently picking one as the de-facto Linux standard -- the same one-key-can't-hold-two-shapes problem `posix` vs `macos` already solved one level up. `install.linux.apt` is REQUIRED and, like install.macos, its tool-name keys must exactly equal `prerequisites.posix` (the Debian/Ubuntu-family default every existing consumer already depends on). `install.linux.dnf` is OPTIONAL and, when present, its tool-name keys must be a SUBSET of `prerequisites.posix` -- NOT required to be complete: a dnf-family tool this manifest cannot verify (issue #1464's hard bar -- a container job actually running the command and confirming the binary lands on PATH is the only admission ticket) is left OUT of the map entirely rather than guessed, and every consumer (bootstrap.sh's PREREQ_HINT_DNF, tan's `_resolve_install_commands`) already degrades an absent per-tool entry to a host-neutral, package-manager-agnostic hint instead of a broken command -- the exact discipline issue #949 established for a tool with no install command on ANY OS at all, now also available at the sub-map level. `ninja` is the first live case: Fedora's own repos carry `ninja-build`, but the RHEL-derivative default repos (measured on rockylinux:9 -- BaseOS/AppStream/Extras, no EPEL) do not carry `ninja`/`ninja-build` under any name, so `sudo dnf install -y ninja-build` is DEMONSTRABLY not a `dnf`-ecosystem-uniform command the way the other five are -- `install.linux.dnf` therefore has no `ninja` key, by design, not by omission. `pacman` (Arch) is deliberately NOT a key here at all: an unattended `pacman -S <pkg>` against a sync database staler than the target system risks a partial upgrade (a known way to break an Arch install), and no single command is both safe-unattended and reliable against an unknown-staleness real host -- absent, with the CONSUMER expected to print a host-neutral hint (never a guessed pacman command), is the correct data for that ecosystem today. Deliberately NO distro-ID layer inside `install.linux.dnf` either (e.g. no `rockylinux`/`fedora` split) -- a package-manager key is confirmable on an unknown host (`command -v dnf`) where a distro ID is fuzzy (derivatives, stripped containers); add one only once a name genuinely diverges WITHIN the dnf ecosystem for a tool this manifest still ships (today's one divergence -- ninja -- is handled by leaving it unshipped, not by adding a distro split for it).

linux.description: Keyed by PACKAGE MANAGER (issue #1464), not by tool and not by distro -- see prerequisites.install's own description above for the full rationale (why 'linux' can't be one flat tool map the way 'macos'/'windows' are, why `apt` is required-and-complete while `dnf` is optional-and-partial, and why there is no `pacman` key).

apt.description: One shell install command per prerequisites.posix tool, `sudo apt-get install -y <pkg>`-shaped -- the same command style nativeLibHints.linux.command already uses, so the manifest stays internally consistent. REQUIRED to cover every prerequisites.posix tool (scripts/check_bootstrap_manifest.py enforces exact-key-equality here, the same bar install.macos already meets).

dnf.description: One `sudo dnf install -y <pkg>` command per prerequisites.posix tool THIS MANIFEST CAN VERIFY on the dnf ecosystem (Fedora + RHEL-family) -- a SUBSET of prerequisites.posix, not required to be complete. A tool with no entry here (today: `ninja` -- see prerequisites.install's own description for why) is absent BY DESIGN; every consumer treats an absent per-tool entry as 'print a host-neutral hint', never as licence to guess.

macos.description: One shell install command per prerequisites.posix tool, `brew install <pkg>`-shaped -- the same command style nativeLibHints.macos.command already uses.

windows.description: One `winget install -e --id <PackageId>` command per prerequisites.windows tool, copied VERBATIM from scripts/bootstrap.ps1's own hardcoded $Prereqs Hint= values for that (GATED) tool -- those values remain the authority for a gated tool (bootstrap.ps1 cannot read this file to print its own prereq-missing hint; see prerequisites' own description above), and scripts/check_bootstrap_manifest.py asserts the two agree byte-for-byte. MAY also carry a command for a tool with no matching prerequisites.windows gate and no $Prereqs entry at all (issue #1036's `7zip`; see prerequisites.install's own description above for why) -- such a tool is exempt from the $Prereqs byte-for-byte check, since bootstrap.ps1 never prompts for it.

artifactProvenance.description: ADR 0021 §3's one-consent-screen facts (issue #1574) -- itemising artifact / source / size / licence per tier, so the IDE can render that screen without a hardcoded downstream allowlist keyed on tool name (alplabai/alp-sdk-vscode#467 names that shortcut explicitly and forbids it: 'If the producer cannot express it yet, that is an upstream issue to file' -- this is that issue). Keyed by the SAME tool-name string `prerequisites.install` already uses across `install.linux.apt` / `install.linux.dnf` / `install.macos` / `install.windows` -- the union of those maps' keys, not a synthetic OS-independent id: `python3` (posix/macos) and `python` (windows) are the same upstream CPython project and so carry near-identical entries under two keys, the same choice `prerequisites.install` already made rather than inventing a canonical id this manifest has never had. scripts/check_bootstrap_manifest.py's `_check_artifact_provenance` asserts this key set stays exactly that union, so a tool added to any install.* map without a matching entry here (or a stale entry for a tool no install.* map still names) fails the gate instead of drifting silently -- the same bar `_check_install_commands` already holds `prerequisites.posix/macos/windows` to, one level further out. Every entry here today is tier A: every prerequisite this manifest ships an install command for is delivered by a signed, user-scope package manager (winget/apt/dnf/brew) -- no elevation, one consent click -- per the ADR 0021 §3 table's own footnote that delivery mechanism (package manager vs hermetic archive) and elevation are independent axes. No tier B (J-Link/WinUSB drivers, udev rules, WSL2 enablement) or tier C (DEEPX DX-M1, vendor NPU compilers) artifact is declared ANYWHERE in metadata/bootstrap.json yet -- neither exists as an install-command entry here today, so there is nothing yet to attach these facts to; adding one is a separate, larger change (a new install surface, not just new facts about an existing one) left to a follow-up issue, not invented here. The Zephyr SDK / `arm-zephyr-eabi` toolchain -- also tier A per the ADR table -- is DELIBERATELY NOT duplicated in here either: its source (`baseUrl`+`filename`) and sizeBytes already live, per-host, in metadata/toolchains.json's `zephyrSdk.artifacts[]` (the pinned-hermetic-archive case this key's own `sizeBytes`/`source` descriptions below contrast themselves against) -- restating them here would be a second copy of the same fact to drift, and that file's own tier/licence facts are left to a follow-up rather than bundled into this issue's file scope. This is producer-only data today: no script in this repo reads it yet (see `_PRODUCER_ONLY_LEAF_PREFIX` in the gate) -- forwarding it through `tan doctor --json` is deliberately left to a companion tan-cli issue, filed only once this shape has proven itself, not described here as a shape nothing downstream has verified yet.

pipSpec.description: The west pip floor Zephyr's own requirements-base.txt declares ('Keep the version identical to the minimum required in cmake/modules/west.cmake'). This IS the exact spec both bootstrap scripts pip-install west with (`pip install --upgrade -q <pipSpec>`) -- not merely informational; bump this value to change the floor both scripts install.

initArgs.description: Static flags for `west <initArgs...> <repo-root>` (the repo-root argument is supplied by the executor, not baked in here).

updateArgs.description: Full argv (after `west`) for the shallow+narrow `west update` both scripts run.

extensionGuardCommand.description: The alp-* extension-command substring (issue #769) both scripts grep for in `west help` output to confirm the workspace's manifest really is alp-sdk's west.yml.

bootstrapUpgrade.description: Packages `pip install --upgrade -q` bootstraps into the fresh venv before anything else.

sdkExtras.description: alp-sdk-side pip extras installed into the workspace venv (jsonschema for scripts/alp_project.py, imgtool for the MCUboot dev-key script).

editableInstall.description: Target `pip install -e <target>` installs -- the ${SDK_ROOT}-tokened alp-sdk checkout, including the SDK's internal/reference `alp_cli` library modules (used by scripts/validate_board_yaml.py and friends, not a command-line front door of their own) and surviving west commands.

verdict.description: The single source for the closing-verdict rule (issue #1038 / tan-cli#220): each pip-install phase below stays non-fatal in itself -- the workspace is left on disk regardless of which packages failed -- but a run that hit one of `blockingPhases` has NOT produced an environment that can do what it was bootstrapped for, and must not report unqualified success. Both SDK bootstrap scripts read this object; Python Tan mirrors the identical three phase IDs independently in `python/tan/commands/bootstrap_cmd.py::WORKSPACE_BLOCKING` -- tan does not read this manifest key, so keeping the declarations in sync across repos remains a by-hand contract, not a mechanically-gated one.

blockingPhases.description: The `pip` sub-step identifiers (matching the `code` argument each script's warn-call site tags itself with -- `zephyr-requirements`, `sdk-extras`, `editable-install`) after which the closing verdict must not be an unqualified success. Deliberately excludes `pip-upgrade`: the pip already present still installs packages, so a failed pip/wheel self-upgrade is cosmetic, not blocking.

partialNoteTemplate.description: Printed as a second line under a still-successful 'Bootstrap complete.' when --allow-partial was passed and blockingPhases is non-empty. The literal token `{{PHASES}}` is replaced with the comma-joined list of the phases that actually failed this run (a subset of blockingPhases, not the whole list) -- substituted by each script itself, not by any token both scripts already share (${SDK_ROOT}/${WORKSPACE_DIR}), since this substitution is run-dependent, not a fixed path.

incompleteMessageTemplate.description: The closing message when blockingPhases is non-empty and --allow-partial was NOT passed -- the run exits non-zero. Same `{{PHASES}}` substitution as partialNoteTemplate.

incompleteRemedy.description: The remedy line printed alongside incompleteMessageTemplate, naming both ways out (fix the failed installs and re-run, or accept the workspace as-is with --allow-partial).

ZEPHYR_BASE.description: ${WORKSPACE_DIR}-tokened path to the Zephyr tree a consumer should export ZEPHYR_BASE as.

ZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT.description: The toolchain variant both bootstrap scripts export alongside ZEPHYR_BASE.

nativeLibHints.description: Per-OS hints for the optional native libraries the Yocto-side backends need -- an apt/brew/pkg-manager fact, printed under a heading about OPTIONAL NATIVE LIBRARIES. Does NOT carry the Arm GNU Toolchain / Zephyr SDK manual-install sentence (see manualInstallHints below): that fact is not about a native library and was pulled out after it was found printing under this key's 'native libraries' heading when bootstrap.sh ran under git-bash (issue #917 review).

manualInstallHints.description: Manual, one-time install steps a script cannot automate for itself (a GUI/EXE installer, or a step that only makes sense from an already-assembled workspace) -- distinct from nativeLibHints (an apt/brew/pkg-manager command bootstrap CAN hand the user verbatim). Both `windows` and `posix` carry the same two facts (the Zephyr SDK, and the conditionally-needed Arm GNU Toolchain), NOT peer facts within either key: the Zephyr SDK (providing `arm-zephyr-eabi`, what the Zephyr-on-M real-silicon path actually builds with) is what every Zephyr customer needs; the Arm GNU Toolchain (`arm-none-eabi-gcc`) is conditional -- needed by three opt-in paths (rebuilding the optional, open GD32 bridge firmware; building the CC3501E bridge firmware's silicon-free stub target; or hand-writing bare-metal firmware for a real M-class core), none of them the Zephyr-on-M default. `windows`'s note also records that the Zephyr SDK's Windows bundle ships neither `dtc` nor `gperf` (unlike its Linux bundle, which does ship `dtc`), so both need their own separate install too on native Windows -- `posix` has no such caveat (`dtc`/`gperf` come from the same apt/brew line nativeLibHints already covers, or ship with the Zephyr SDK's Linux hosttools). Both are printed under a 'NOT auto-installed (manual, one-time)' heading -- bootstrap.ps1 for `windows`, bootstrap.sh for `posix` (issue #949 addendum A4 -- `posix` used to be absent, so no Linux/macOS hint could ever render).

note.description: One or more human-readable lines, safe to print verbatim under a MANUAL-install heading (not the native-library apt/brew heading nativeLibHints.*.note prints under).

One or more human-readable lines, safe to print verbatim under bootstrap.sh's MANUAL-install heading. Shared by Linux and macOS (bootstrap.sh doesn't split posix by OS here the way nativeLibHints does -- the two facts this key carries don't have OS-specific commands worth splitting over).

tier.description: ADR 0021 §3's consent-screen tier. A -- hermetic or signed-package-manager delivered, no elevation: install after one consent click. B -- needs elevation (drivers, udev rules, WSL2 enablement): prompt once, stay skippable, and show the command that will run rather than only executing it. C -- licence-gated third party: never silently fetched, show the licence, then verify. A property of the ARTIFACT, not of any one consumer's opinion -- the reason issue #1574 exists is so an IDE never has to hardcode this per tool name.

source.description: The artifact's canonical upstream origin -- its project homepage or source repository -- NOT a per-version download URL. Every entry today is delivered by a signed, user-scope package manager (winget/apt/dnf/brew), which resolves its OWN download URL per host, architecture, and already-installed version, so no single fixed download URL exists to pin here the way metadata/toolchains.json's `baseUrl` does for the pinned, hermetic Zephyr SDK archives.

sizeBytes.description: Approximate download size in bytes, or null. null here is the honest answer, not an unresearched gap: every entry today is package-manager-resolved, and a package manager's own download size varies by host OS, CPU architecture, and whichever version is already cached or partially installed -- there is no single number that would be true across hosts. Contrast metadata/toolchains.json's `zephyrSdk.artifacts[].sizeBytes`, which IS a fixed, sha256-verified figure, because that artifact is a pinned hermetic archive fetched from one exact URL regardless of host.

licence.description: SPDX licence identifier for the artifact's primary licence, or null. null means the upstream project's licensing is genuinely multi-component (more than one licence covers different files/modules of the same distributed artifact) and cannot be honestly reduced to a single SPDX id without a file-level audit this repo has not performed -- an absent value, not a guessed one, per issue #1574's own instruction that a fabricated licence string is worse than an absent one. A non-null value is a real, verifiable fact about the named upstream project.

note.description: One or more human-readable lines, safe to print verbatim -- an ARRAY (not one long paragraph) so both scripts can render an aligned, multi-line mapping instead of an unwrapped ~200-380 char line.

command.description: A single copy-pasteable shell command, or null when the OS has no equivalent install command (e.g. native Windows).
